title: The Limits of Scale: Why a Massive Teacher Coaching Program Produced Zero Gains
author: Ammar A. Merhbi
summary: Ammar Merhbi reviews a study in Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis of a large urban district's Instructor Coaching Program, which hired nearly 1,000 teachers as part-time coaches for more than 6,000 mentees across about 130 schools between 2014 and 2022. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design, the researchers found null effects on teacher retention and on English and math achievement, with math estimates leaning negative, at a cost above $20 million a year. Merhbi identifies three mechanisms: the talent pool thinned as the program scaled, pulling high performers from classrooms carried an instructional cost, and coaches increasingly gave summative evaluations, which breeds defensiveness and cut observation frequency. The researchers note a general 10 percent raise might have reduced turnover more. His practical takeaways are to wall off coaching from evaluation, scale only as far as elite talent allows, and ruthlessly protect coaching time.
points: A coaching program with nearly 1,000 coaches and over $20 million a year produced no measurable gains in teacher retention or student achievement.
As the program scaled, the district drafted merely effective teachers as coaches, diluting the expertise behind the feedback.
Coaches also rated about 80 percent of their mentees, which blurs formative support with summative judgment and invites defensiveness.
Observations per mentee fell from about five a year to two or three as administrative duties grew.
School leaders should separate coaching from evaluation, scale within the talent pool, and protect time for observation and feedback.
quotes: The findings were statistically null across all primary metrics. The program did not increase teacher retention at the school or district level.

The researchers point out that applying this budget toward a general 10% salary increase for all teachers would likely have reduced teacher turnover far more effectively than the coaching program did.
As the program expanded universally to cover 130 schools, the talent pool thinned.
By 2022, approximately 80% of mentee teachers received their summative professionalism ratings directly from their coaches.
First, instructional coaching must be structurally walled off from summative evaluation.

If you are forced to draft merely average or “effective” teachers into coaching roles just to fill a master schedule, the math will fail, and overall student achievement will suffer from their absence in the classroom.
